clean_source_blocks.text: US envoys Jared Kushner (left) and Steve Witkoff Two US envoys are hoping for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war, US officials say. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, having "discussed substantive plans for next steps" with Putin on Saturday, according to the White House. It is not yet clear exactly what they are, but an announcement is expected in the coming weeks, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace. It will be to the first trip by US President Donald Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner leave Moscow talks with hopes for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine.

‘Substantive plans’ will be announced in ‘coming weeks’ as envoys head to Kyiv for talks with Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy Donald Trump’s envoys “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war between Ukraine and Russia during their meeting on Saturday in Moscow with Vladimir Putin, the White House said. Those steps would be announced in “coming weeks”, a White House official said in a statement, and the envoys “look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow [Sunday] in Ukraine”. Moscow said the US envoys had proposed a “number of ideas” on how to end the Ukraine war in “extremely frank” talks with the Russian president in the Kremlin late on Saturday. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the Americans “put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement”, on which he did not elaborate.

Fresh talks in Moscow about the Ukraine war between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have come to an end three hours after they began, according to state media reports on Saturday. US President Donald Trump's envoys left the Kremlin late in the evening, in a motorcade shown in state media. No details have yet emerged about the content or outcome of the talks. Earlier, the Kremlin said the public would be briefed following the meeting. Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law were set to travel onwards to Kiev, where Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is due to welcome the two. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the US negotiators had brought new proposals with them, without providing any details. Trump had also said that Witkoff and Kushner were bringing a proposal.

US envoys Jared Kushner (left) and Steve Witkoff

Two US envoys are hoping for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war, US officials say.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, having "discussed substantive plans for next steps" with Putin on Saturday, according to the White House.

It is not yet clear exactly what they are, but an announcement is expected in the coming weeks, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace.

It will be to the first trip by US President Donald Trump's top negotiators to  Ukraine's capital. Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days.

Watch: President Putin welcomes US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to talks in Moscow

As Witkoff and Kushner were negotiating at the Kremlin, Zelensky said he was ready for "a substantive conversation".

Saturday's talks in Moscow lasted three hours and were held behind closed doors in Putin's official residence in the heart of the Russian capital, according to Russian state media.

Details are still emerging, but both sides have given broadly positive remarks without going into specifics.

Putin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the talks as "constructive, extremely frank".

"The talks were not limited to an exchange of views on resolving the Ukrainian crisis - economic issues and potential major, mutually beneficial Russian-American projects were discussed in considerable detail," he said.

Ushakov also said "note was made of the Russian army's tangible advances in the combat zone" and that there was acknowledgement that talks needed to address "the root causes of the conflict".

Despite an escalation of Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukrainian cities including Kyiv, Russian ground forces have made very slow advances for most of the conflict, incurring enormous casualties. Russia still controls about one-fifth of Ukrainian territory - areas that it seized back in 2022.

Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times but given Ukraine's airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, it is not clear how they will be travelling to Kyiv from Moscow.

The talks come after Russia and Ukraine have intensified aerial attacks in recent months.

‘Substantive plans’ will be announced in ‘coming weeks’ as envoys head to Kyiv for talks with Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy

Donald Trump’s envoys “discussed substantive plans for next steps” for ending the war between Ukraine and Russia during their meeting on Saturday in Moscow with Vladimir Putin, the White House said.

Those steps would be announced in “coming weeks”, a White House official said in a statement, and the envoys “look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow [Sunday] in Ukraine”.

Moscow said the US envoys had proposed a “number of ideas” on how to end the Ukraine war in “extremely frank” talks with the Russian president in the Kremlin late on Saturday.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the Americans “put forward a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement”, on which he did not elaborate.

Ushakov said Russia had told the US envoys that Moscow was “confident” it could achieve its military goals of seizing the rest of eastern Ukraine, in comments implying the Kremlin’s stance on its war against Ukraine had not changed.

Meanwhile, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Russian attacks on Kyiv and Boryspil international airports – which service the Ukrainian capital – were “clearly” a reaction to the possibility of the US negotiators flying to Kyiv after the talks in Moscow.

Zelenskyy on Saturday said Kyiv had “taken note of this Russian move, and next week we will adjust our operation accordingly regarding Russian airspace, which has become dangerous because of our drones and missiles in the sky”.

“Of course, there are and will be no threats to diplomacy from our side.”

Officials visiting Ukraine have largely done so by train, as Ukrainian airspace has been closed since 2022 due to the war.

Russia and Ukraine had vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during the negotiations, as Washington tries to revive US-led talks to end Europe’s worst conflict since the second world war.

The Moscow visit came as Donald Trump suggested on Friday he had a new proposal to end the war, without providing any details. Trump made ending the war a priority early in his second term, but little has changed so far.

Trump said his son-in-law Kushner and business ally Witkoff were bringing “a proposal to end the war”.
